transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Hi. Well, I guess what brings me in is that I keep getting up when I'm supposed to just stay put. It's happening a lot lately. Like, during client interviews, or tutoring sessions... even at my book club. People are really starting to notice that I can't just sit and listen. I just have to get out of my chair. So, I figured I should probably come in and talk to someone about it.
Did these problems with getting up and not staying seated also happen when you were a child?

Yes, they actually did. Um, if you look at my grade-school report cards, they always said that I was bright, but that I just couldn't stay in my seat or wait my turn. My mother actually still jokes about it today. She says I treated every classroom like a crime scene that I had to pace through. So, yeah, it's definitely been happening since I was a kid.
Do you often get into arguments with authority figures or deliberately refuse to follow rules or requests?

No, not really. I mean, I don't have any issues with authority figures or anything like that. I follow the rules just fine. I might have a hard time sitting still, but I'm not deliberately refusing to do what I'm told or picking fights with people in charge.
Do you often have trouble paying close attention to details or making careless mistakes in your work or daily tasks?

No, I don't think so. I'm actually pretty good with details. In my line of work, you really have to be. I don't really make careless mistakes or lose focus on the facts of a case, I just... I just have a hard time staying in my chair while I'm looking at them.
Do you often have trouble staying focused on what someone is saying to you?

No, I wouldn't say that. I'm actually pretty good at listening to people. When I'm interviewing a witness or a client, I'm completely tuned in to what they're saying. I don't really space out or lose the thread of the conversation. I just might be tapping my foot or shifting around while I listen.
